question: For the five pinned sign-changing zero-shell roots of the declared raw-C Gamma_1,p=0 extension, do bounded numerical controls support local simplicity and, conditional on the declared moving-boundary Wronskian/Lagrange identity, what local delta(C) Jacobian 1/|d lambda_j/dp| follows?

upstream_results.role: pins exactly five declared finite-window characteristic roots and their p-branch convention; it does not supply spectral weights or RAQ

primary_sources.source: I. S. Gradshteyn and I. M. Ryzhik, Table of Integrals, Series, and Products, 8th ed., formula 6.576(4)
primary_sources.used_for: the Mellin integral int_0^infinity x^(mu-1)K_nu(x)^2 dx used to normalize the declared weighted Lagrange identity
primary_sources.not_used_for: a full spectral theorem, raw-C rigging map, or C/H equivalence

primary_sources.source: T. Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, Springer (1995 reprint)
primary_sources.used_for: the domain-dependence warning behind not applying a naive fixed-domain Hellmann-Feynman formula
primary_sources.not_used_for: proving that this one raw-C extension is physically selected

primary_sources.source: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, modified Bessel functions, sections 10.25, 10.29 and 10.40
primary_sources.used_for: the zero-shell K_(i*kappa) convention and numerical evaluation of the characteristic derivative
primary_sources.not_used_for: positivity of a physical Hilbert product or observable action

declared_conventions.p_branch: p>0 for reported lambda_prime; p<0 has the opposite slope because the declared spectrum is even in p

assumptions: the pinned census roots are treated as the five declared local root centers; this calculation does not claim an exhaustive root classification outside its fixed prior census
the generalized fiber equation is L_p u=lambda f u with the declared Gamma_1,p=0 boundary line and plus-end solution continuation
the Wronskian/Lagrange identity includes the p-dependent boundary-domain contribution through F_lambda and is the declared route to the local slope

the runner does not construct a nonzero-lambda plus-end Weyl solution or independently finite-difference F_lambda; every reported lambda slope and delta(C) Jacobian is conditional on the stated moving-boundary Lagrange identity and its hypotheses
N_f is positive for a nonzero real u_0 and finite because the f-weight becomes a z^(1/2) Mellin integrand
the optional bounded log-z quadrature is an independent numerical cross-check of the Mellin formula, not a replacement for endpoint/domain analysis

the naive fixed-domain Hellmann-Feynman expression based on integral |u_0|^2 dQ is not used: it diverges at the limit-circle minus end for K_(i*kappa), and it omits the p-dependent boundary-domain contribution
tasks: hash-verify the five-root census result and recover its root centers
derive the Wronskian/Lagrange formula F_lambda(0)=-N_f/(2*hbar^2*a) and the positive-p slope lambda_prime=2*hbar^2*a*F_p/N_f
reduce N_f to the stated z Mellin integral and evaluate its gamma-function closed form
compute F_kappa with centered-step refinement, a, N_f, conditional F_lambda, conditional lambda_prime and conditional 1/abs(lambda_prime) for each of the five pinned roots

check refined nonzero F_kappa, N_f, conditional F_lambda and conditional lambda slope, verify slope signs and the opposite negative-p branch slope, and cross-check N_f and complex leakage by five bounded log-z quadratures
leave global spectral measure, rigging test space/map, physical positivity, observable action, RAQ completion and C/H equivalence null

decision_table.condition: the upstream five-root pin, Mellin normalization, explicitly conditional local Lagrange identity guard, refined nonzero simple-root checks, slope parity and bounded quadrature cross-checks all pass
any upstream, Mellin, identity, simplicity, slope or quadrature control fails
